audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects raises it directly: Riven wins 55.42% over 1005 games but the chart hands Lillia the majority of stages, and the page rates the lane TRICKY at 7.5/10.
audit.why: The chart is right — Lillia genuinely owns Levels 3 through First item, and the whys already say so in detail. The difficulty rating is the number that looks out of step with a 55% win rate; the mirror settled on 5/10 from Lillia's side. I did not flip diffRating because that number also drives diff, tone and four report strings, and getting it wrong changes the whole page's colour.
audit.corrected: Chart corrected (point 3). diffRating left at 7.5/10 and raised as a question for the user rather than guessed at.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows were inverted against both the packet and the whys printed directly underneath them. The page said Riven wins Level 3, Levels 4-5 and First item while whys[2] says she 'stays outside your W stun range for the entire trade', whys[3] says 'she kites the all-in and you cannot pin her', and whys[5] says 'you cannot sustain through it'. Level 1 said Lillia while whys[0] says 'you win every level-1 skirmish'.
audit.why: This is the exact failure mode the chart check exists for: the prose was right and the sides were the opposite of the prose, so a reader got two contradictory answers on the same row. The mirror resolved to Riven / Skill / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia / Skill and the packet agrees.
audit.corrected: Whole chart proposed as one atomic group in matched full/content pairs: row 0 -> Riven, rows 2, 3 and 5 -> Lillia, row 6 -> Skill. Ratings walked to 7, 6, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5 — the exact inverse of the mirror's 3, 4, 7, 7, 7, 7, 5. Rows 1 and 4 already agreed. No why text needed changing: every row now matches the reason already printed beneath it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly describes a 'W bounce' — 'she bounces W through you' (whys[2]), 'W bounce-speed' (spikes[1]), 'W-bounce trade patterns' (spikes[3]), 'her W bounce plus Blooming Blows passive move speed' (mid), 'bouncing W through you' (wants.foe[0]). Watch Out! Eep! is a stationary area hit that does heavy damage in the centre; nothing about it bounces. The move speed the page attributes to the bounce is actually Blooming Blows' passive, which stacks whenever she hits anything with a spell.
audit.why: The player is being told to dodge a bounce arc that does not exist, and to track the wrong ability for her kiting. The real number to play around is Blooming Blows: 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s on a 450 range, against Riven's 260-range Ki Burst — that gap, not a bounce, is why she stays out of the stun.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[1].text and wants.foe[0] rewritten with the real source of the move speed and the real cooldown and range numbers. The remaining 'bounce' references in mid, late and spikes[3] are flagged in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells the player part of Lillia's damage ignores resistances.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags resistances-invalidated: Blooming Blows deals extra TRUE damage on its outer edge. The page's itemization sends her to Mercury's Treads and generic MR, which does nothing against the edge damage — health is the stat that reads this trade correctly, and staying out of the rim rather than stacking a resist is the actual play.
audit.corrected: True damage on the edge written into whys[2], wants.foe[0], dosFull[0].d and report[5].t, with the explicit 'buy HP, not MR' call in the interactions line.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flags 'Laden Bough' in spikes[1]. False positive — the page writes 'Dream-Laden Bough (passive)', which is exactly right; the detector matched on the truncated substring.
audit.corrected: No change; recorded so it is not chased again.

questionsForUser: Riven vs Lillia (top), field diff / diffRating in the full layer: the page rates this TRICKY at 7.5/10 while Riven wins 55.42% over 1005 games, and the mirror agent set Lillia's side to 5/10 difficulty and 6.5/10 carry threat. packet.defects flags the contradiction explicitly. Should diffRating drop to 5/10 and diff move from TRICKY to EVEN — which would also mean changing tone, breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t — or does the lane genuinely play harder than its win rate suggests and the rating stays?
notes: Three 'W bounce' references I did not touch, because each sits inside a long prose block whose surrounding advice I could not rewrite within the length band without cutting something verified: spikes[3].text, mid and late. They should be swept when someone next edits those blocks. Left unverified and deliberately unaltered: the claim that Lilting Lullaby sleeps for 1.5 seconds (whys[4], mid) and that 'three stacks let her R from range' (early). Riot's text gives neither a duration nor a stack threshold — it says only that enemies with Dream Dust become Drowsy before falling asleep — so I left both alone rather than invent or delete a number I cannot check.
